ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a benzene ring connected to an NH2 group; on the right side is a benzene ring connected to an aldehyde/protonated carbonyl fragment, the carbonyl carbon is also connected to an H, and the oxygen is connected to an H and bears a positive charge. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: As required, exclude all bonds involving hydrogen. In the left component, the benzene ring has 6 C-C bonds, and the bond from the benzene-ring carbon to N has 1 non-hydrogen bond, for a total of 7. In the right component, the benzene ring has 6 C-C bonds, the C-C bond from the benzene ring to the carbonyl carbon has 1, and the C=O bond is counted as 1 bond; C-H and O-H bonds are excluded, so the right side has a total of 8. The total is 7 + 8 = 15.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First count the left component: the benzene ring has 6 C-C bonds, and the bond from the ring carbon to N in NH2 adds 1 non-H bond, giving 7. Then count the right component: the phenyl ring has 6 C-C bonds, the bond from the phenyl ring to the carbonyl carbon adds 1, and the C=O bond adds 1; exclude the C-H and O-H bonds. The right component gives 8. Add 7 + 8 to obtain 15.
